name: int-format
axis: integer to decimal string, then reading the produced digits back
notes: n = integers formatted. VL uses the `toString(i32)` builtin, JS `String(v)`, Rust `v.to_string()`, Python `str(v)`. One value in five is negative so the sign path is exercised. The LCG stays below 10^6 so the value sequence is exact in every runtime at any N. Python runs N=1_000_000, a 30x reduction. There is NO opt.vl: `toString` is already the fastest VL spelling - a hand-rolled digit loop through fromCodePoints measured 4.4x SLOWER. stdfmt.vl is a non-optimised VARIANT that swaps the builtin for std:fmt's pure-VL `toStr()`, to price the library renderer (5.7x slower than the builtin); `toStr` is the only option for i64, which the builtin refuses.
